object_description: permeable perimeter crown around a compact school volume
design_condition: The school occupies the northwestern edge of the block interior, preserving existing operations while forming a green heart connected to surrounding streets and paths.

positive.statement: The permeable built front adapts particularly well to the surrounding context.
The location provides a particularly relevant operational solution by allowing existing facilities to remain in use.
The school’s placement makes clever and economical use of the triangular block while maximizing surrounding green space.
The clear alignments and simple whole fit naturally into the preserved environment.
The school is connected clearly to the neighborhood by primary and secondary paths.
The south-side passageways successfully combine sun protection, escape routes, and exterior courtyard areas.

negative.statement: The jury considers that a semi-buried parking installation would better protect the overall composition.
The generous crossing hall is cluttered to the point of saturation, and the stair flights appear undersized.
The ground floor is particularly dark.
The additional classroom and very large hall tend to inflate the volume to be built.
The future of the preserved plane-tree mall and the proposed concentration of play equipment require reconsideration.
